name: Sitagliptin
drafted_by: AI-assisted draft (Claude) for review by Dr. W. Rivero

usual_adult_dose.dose: 100 mg once daily; 50 mg if eGFR 30 to <45; 25 mg if eGFR <30 (including dialysis)

key_interactions.action: Lower insulin or secretagogue doses may be needed.

common: Upper respiratory tract infection, nasopharyngitis, headache (≥5% and more than placebo)
serious: Acute renal failure, sometimes requiring dialysis (postmarketing)
Serious hypersensitivity (anaphylaxis, angioedema, exfoliative skin reactions)

contraindications: History of serious hypersensitivity to sitagliptin (e.g., anaphylaxis, angioedema)
monitoring: Kidney function before starting and periodically (dose by eGFR)
Signs of heart failure in at-risk patients

pk.half_life_eskd: Not reported; AUC about 4-fold higher in severe impairment including ESRD on hemodialysis (label)
pk.metabolism: Minor (about 16% as metabolites); CYP3A4 with CYP2C8
pk.excretion_renal_pct: About 79% unchanged in urine (active tubular secretion; OAT3, P-gp)
pk.dialyzability: Modestly: about 13.5% removed over a 3- to 4-hour hemodialysis; PD removal unknown (label).

sources.citation: Merck Sharp & Dohme LLC. (2024). JANUVIA (sitagliptin) [Prescribing information; US FDA-approved label, NDA021995, set ID f85a48d0-0407-4c50-b0fa-7673a160bf01, version effective November 14, 2024]. DailyMed, U.S. National Library of Medicine.
